office_does: The treasurer collects property taxes and safeguards, invests and accounts for county and district funds. The treasurer does not set tax rates.
race_blurb: Open seat. Wealth advisor Rick Viall, a first-time candidate, led the primary 53% to 47% over Doug Miller, a former assistant fire chief who has served on the Wenatchee City Council, school board and a fire commission. Both stress safeguarding public funds and accountability.

candidates.summary: Chelan County wealth advisor and business owner, a first-time candidate running on fiduciary stewardship, audit preparation and modern financial systems.
highlights: Would improve coordination with the Auditor, strengthen audit preparation and update financial software [S1]
Says the treasurer collects, safeguards and accounts for taxes but does not decide them [S5]
Campaign site offers property-tax lookup tools and a stress test of the port authority's Malaga bond plan [S5][S7]

experience.basis: Has never held elected office; runs on private-sector fiduciary and compliance experience.

spending.basis: Stresses audit preparation, strict investment-policy compliance and fiduciary controls, and questions whether the port needs new revenue tools rather than better use of existing assets.

candidates.summary: Former assistant fire chief and airline pilot with a long record in local elected office, including the Wenatchee City Council, running on his public-office experience and protection of public funds.
highlights: Has served on the Wenatchee School District board, the Wenatchee City Council and a county fire commission [S1]
Elected unopposed to Wenatchee City Council District 2 in 2025 [S6][S9]
Says 'accountability upgrades and cybersecurity' will be his first priority [S1]

experience.basis: Long-serving local elected official who runs on his years in public office, though not an incumbent in this office.
